messages:
jane_cust: Hey team — after migrating traffic to our VPC endpoint for redwood API (vpce-abc123) we're seeing intermittent 502s from services that sit behind our NATGW. ~10% of /v1/complete calls fail with `502 Bad Gateway`. Any ideas?
sarah_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the endpoint DNS you hit and a short curl output (verbose)? Also which AZ is the endpoint in vs your NAT?
jane_cust: DNS: `api.internal.redwood.example` -> resolves to `vpce-abc123-eni-1` (10.0.2.15). Sample: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer X" https://api.internal.redwood.example/v1/complete` returns `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`. From tcpdump on client side I see: `SYN` -> `SYN,ACK` -> `RST` from 10.0.2.15 to ephemeral client port.
alex_sre: Quick checklist: NACL ephemeral ports allowed? ENI SG rules on the endpoint? Endpoint policy restricting principals? Route table associatons?
jane_cust: NACL allows 1024-32768 (we thought ephemeral was lower). SG on endpoint only allows 443 from our VPC CIDR. Endpoint policy was added to only allow a role ARN in our account.
dmitri_infra: Two likely culprits: 1) NACL too narrow (stateless) causing return traffic blocked when ephemeral >32768 2) Endpoint policy or SG blocking the backchannel. Also if your endpoint ENI is in an AZ different from NAT, replies can traverse different path so NACLs matter.
sarah_support: Can you paste the endpoint policy snippet?
jane_cust: Policy we attached: ```json
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {
      "Effect":"Allow",
      "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/ServiceRole"},
      "Action":"execute-api:Invoke",
      "Resource":"*"
    }
  ]
}
```
alex_sre: That is too strict for PrivateLink/API Gateway style setups. The recommended pattern is to allow `Principal: "*"` and restrict by `Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:SourceVpce": "vpce-abc123"}}` so the call must originate from your VPCE. Example: ```json
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {
      "Effect":"Allow",
      "Principal":"*",
      "Action":"execute-api:Invoke",
      "Resource":"arn:aws:execute-api:us-east-1:123456789012:*/prod/*",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:SourceVpce": "vpce-abc123"}}
    }
  ]
}
```
dmitri_infra: Also check the endpoint ENI security group egress/ingress — if SG only allows 443 to VPC CIDR but your clients use ephemeral outgoing ports, the ENI must be allowed to send responses back. SGs are stateful but the peer SG must permit ephemeral destination. For NACL, make sure both inbound and outbound ranges include ephemeral ports up to 65535.
sarah_support: Repro steps that helped others: 1) from a client instance behind NAT run `curl --resolve api.internal.redwood.example:443:10.0.2.15 https://api.internal.redwood.example/v1/health -v` 2) run `sudo tcpdump -n host 10.0.2.15 and port 443` and watch for RSTs 3) check the endpoint service logs (NGINX/ALB) for `upstream prematurely closed connection`
jane_cust: Ran tcpdump: confirmed pattern SYN -> SYN/ACK -> RST from 10.0.2.15 to ephemeral ports in the 33000-34000 range. So NACL limiting to 32768 was probably the culprit.
alex_sre: Yep. NACL is stateless so you need to allow the full ephemeral range both directions. Also update endpoint policy as Dmitri suggested.
jane_cust: Changed NACL to allow 1024-65535 inbound/outbound, updated endpoint policy to use `aws:SourceVpce` condition, and added SG rule to explicitly allow ephemeral return traffic from our VPC CIDR.
# after changes
jane_cust: Follow-up: after changes error rate dropped to 0% in 30m of traffic. `curl` returns 200 consistently. Confirmed with tcpdump — no more RSTs. Thanks all! :tada:
sarah_support: Awesome — thanks for the updates and for closing the loop. We'll add a KB snippet for ephemeral NACL + endpoint policy patterns. :thumbsup:
